performance.cutover_observation: 2026-07-31 MMMU validation, 250 multiple-choice single-image questions, MI210 (ROCm0), llama.cpp-experimental build-v8-hip, one arm at a time, `--image-min-tokens 1024` on EVERY arm, prompt cache disabled (`--cache-ram 0`). Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B Q4_K_M `159/250` (63.6%); Qwen2.5-VL-7B Q4_K_M incumbent `131/250` (52.4%); Qwen3-VL-8B Q8_0 `143/250` (57.2%); Qwen3-VL-4B Q8_0 `135/250` (54.0%). Paired exact McNemar over the 250 aligned items: 49 candidate-only-correct vs 21 incumbent-only-correct, two-sided p=0.0011. COSTS, recorded because this swap is not free: decode is ~1.9x SLOWER (112.20 vs 214.54 t/s median, same host, same harness) and VRAM is 2.7x larger (21049 vs 7685 MB). Quality was the binding constraint; speed was not. PARSE-FAIL ASYMMETRY: the candidate produced 17 unparseable answers, the incumbent 0. That asymmetry counts AGAINST the candidate in the score above, so +11.2 pp is a FLOOR. A further 23 candidate answers were truncated at the 2048-token rescue cap and scored wrong.
performance.vl_score_protocol: MMMU-val, 250 multiple-choice single-image questions, MI210 (ROCm0), 2026-07-31. Paired exact McNemar vs Qwen2.5-VL-7B (131/250): +11.2 pp, p=0.0011.
performance.vram_caveat: VRAM grows on first EXECUTION, not at load — the four-model steady state measured 62.59 of 63.98 GiB (1.40 GiB headroom) after each model ran once, vs 61.66 at load. Any budget built from load-time figures runs ~1 GiB optimistic.
